newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland seeks confectionery investment - premier.
newsitem.headline: Queensland seeks confectionery investment - premier.

text.p: Australia's main sugar-producing state, Queensland, was encouraging foreign confectionery manufacturers to set up production in the state, Premier Rob Borbidge said on Tuesday.
Asian demand for confectionery was growing rapidly, he told the annual meeting of the CANEGROWERS grower organisation on Tuesday.

Foreign producers were being especially encouraged to enter into joint ventures with Queensland organisations and a special project team had been established by the state Department of Primary Industries and other government departments, he said.

Three organisations had recently visited Queensland expressing interest, Borbidge said. One was from the neighbouring Australian state of New South Wales, one from Germany and one from the United State, he said.

The Japanese confectionery market was worth A$12 billion alone, he said. Sugar in Japan cost A$1,600-A$1,700 a tonne against A$520 a tonne in Queensland, while milk in Japan was three times more expensive than in Queensland, he said.
A molasses plant had been proposed for Queensland by a Japanese company, he said, without giving details.
